A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same API Pack research. Their full text, figures, tables and appendices are readable and matchable, supporting comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original model fine-tuning, retrieval, scaling, cross-language and Magicoder integration experiments, with results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds larger-scale training results, GPT zero-shot evaluations, and training-data comparisons in Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: The dataset-curation pipeline, instruction generation and filtering, likelihood-based instruction selection, fine-tuning templates, and retrieval procedures remain the same. The five appendix prompts are substantively unchanged. New filtering experiments test variants of the existing pipeline rather than introduce a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 newly uses a ToolBench corpus, described as RapidAPI-only, as alternative training data in Section 5.5. API Pack's four-source, ten-language coverage and three generalization tasks remain unchanged. HumanEval+ and MBPP evaluations are retained in Appendix 9.6 rather than removed.

E2.justification: v3 adds ToolBench-trained and partly unfiltered-data-trained CodeLlama-13B controls in Tables 5–6. GPT-3.5-1106 and GPT-4-1106 also join the zero-shot comparison in Table 3; v1 compared them only under retrieved three-shot prompting. Existing model and Magicoder comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Scaling expands from 20k–100k Python examples to 10k–1M API Pack examples, although the largest run's language composition is unspecified. New protocols include 20k-example training-data comparisons, replacement of 45% of filtered instructions, and GPT zero-shot testing. v3 also corrects the cross-language supplement description from 9,000 to 1,000 examples per language, matching v1's experimental-settings passage; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct tests of training-data source diversity and instruction filtering through the ToolBench comparison and 45% unfiltered-instruction replacement experiment. It also extends training-size sensitivity analysis to 1M examples. Existing retrieval/reranking and cross-language analyses remain, with some moved from the appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for the model comparisons. Additional result rows retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds 10k/1M scaling results, Tables 5–6 controls, and GPT-3.5/GPT-4 zero-shot API-call accuracies of 0.7%/0.1%. Most matched results remain unchanged, including CodeLlama-13B's 49.5% Level 3 retrieved three-shot accuracy in Table 3. However, new Tables 5–6 report 49.1% for the API Pack/filtered reference, creating an unexplained discrepancy.

T1.justification: v1's two illustrative equations for zero-shot and three-shot prompting are omitted, but v3 retains the same setups in prose. This does not change their mathematical substance. Neither version supplies substantive theoretical results, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The central dataset, GPT comparison and cross-language transfer claims remain. v3 extends the highlighted scaling claim from 100k Python examples to 1M API Pack examples. Preserving general coding performance is no longer a headline contribution, although the claim and supporting experiment remain in Appendix 9.6.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations attributing performance differences to source diversity and filtering, and describes the similarity threshold as permitting developer completion of generated calls. It removes the explicit API-name limitation from Section 7 and Table 1, despite retaining that input requirement in Section 3, and drops the argument-augmentation discussion. The filtering interpretation also overlooks Table 6's contrary Level 3 three-shot API-call result.

D1.justification: Appendix 9.2 newly documents test-set selection and training-data exclusions for all three evaluation levels. v3 replaces anonymous repository/source placeholders with concrete addresses, identifies IBM API Hub, and states dataset and code licenses. These improve documentation and access information; the hardware, training hyperparameters and five prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v3 broadens cited coverage of software engineering, recent code models and multilingual benchmarks, including StarCoder 2, Granite code models and HumanEval-XL. Section 2.2 newly distinguishes its task from predefined-function calling, citing NexusRaven, EasyTool and Octopus. Conversely, v1's detailed code-instruction-dataset subsection and WizardCoder discussion are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, dataset description and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Cross-language and scaling sections are reordered, the Magicoder study moves to the appendix, and the separate Future Work section disappears. The title clarifies that multilinguality concerns programming languages, and appendix organization changes substantially.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column layout. v3 expands Table 3, adds Tables 5–6, redraws the scaling figure with an extended range, and resizes cross-language plots. Retrieval and ten-language displays move into the main text, while the Magicoder table moves to the appendix. Code examples and prompt listings are also reformatted.

improvement.justification: The added training-data controls, extended scaling study, explicit split instructions and concrete access/licensing information make v3 better supported and easier to assess and reproduce. The net gain is limited by inconsistent reference scores across Tables 3 and 5–6, Section 5.5's overstated filtering conclusion, and removal of the explicit API-name limitation. These weaknesses temper the useful additions without erasing their overall benefit.
